ei.subject: 공통영어1 미래엔(김성연)
ei.title: The Power of Friendliness: Soft but Strong

fullPassage: I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food.

questions.passage: He explained that dogs, unlike wolves, have developed communicative skills with humans and a sense of friendliness. ① They say that from the common ancestors of these two species, those that acted friendly toward humans evolved into dogs, and those that didn’t became wolves. ② Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably provided them with a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves. ③ I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. ④
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"This explanation sounds reasonable according to several evolutionary biologists."

det.korean: "This explanation"은 Hare 박사가 개의 의사소통 능력과 친밀감에 대해 설명한 것을 가리킨다. 이 설명이 합리적이라고 말한 "several evolutionary biologists"가 바로 다음 문장의 "They"이다.
det.analysis:
✅ ①: "He explained..." 직후 → "This explanation"이 가리킬 대상이 바로 앞에 있고, "They say..."의 "They" = evolutionary biologists
❌ ②: 이미 They의 말이 끝난 후 → This explanation의 지칭 대상이 모호
❌ ③: 새 단락 시작 전 → 흐름 방해
❌ ④: 새 예시 시작 후 → 문맥 불일치
det.tip: "This explanation" → 앞 문장의 설명을 지칭, "They" → 바로 뒤에 나오는 주어와 연결

questions.passage: Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. ① Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. ② One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. ③ These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment. ④
questions.stem:
다음 글에서 주어진 문장이 들어가기에 가장 적절한 곳은?

"Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived."

det.korean: "these attributes"는 네안데르탈인의 도구/불 제작 능력과 강한 신체를 가리킨다. 이 자질에도 "불구하고(Despite)" 호모 사피엔스가 살아남았다는 전환이 와야 한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ②: 네안데르탈인의 강점 서술 직후 → "these attributes" = 도구, 불, 강한 신체 → Despite로 전환
❌ ①: 아직 구체적 자질 나열 전
❌ ③: 이미 설명이 시작된 후
❌ ④: 결론 이후
det.tip: "Despite these attributes" → 앞에 attributes(자질)가 구체적으로 나열되어야 함

questions.passage: Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, __________________________________________ when they cooperate. By being kind and working together, we can truly flourish.
questions.stem:
다음 주어진 단어를 올바른 순서로 배열하시오.

person / each / to / can / world / beautiful / a more / contribute

det.korean: "each person can contribute to a more beautiful world" → 각 사람은 더 아름다운 세상에 기여할 수 있다.
det.analysis:
each person(주어) + can contribute(동사) + to a more beautiful world(전치사구)
조동사 can 뒤 동사원형 contribute, "a more beautiful"이 world를 수식
det.tip: 주어(each person) + 조동사(can) + 동사(contribute) + to + 명사구(a more beautiful world)

questions.wa: each person can contribute to a more beautiful world
accept: each person can contribute to a more beautiful world
Each person can contribute to a more beautiful world

questions.passage: Although the two are ①<u>genetically</u> similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device ②<u>which</u> required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When ③<u>placed</u> with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when ④<u>pairing</u> with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally ⑤<u>succeeded</u>, they did not share the food with their partner.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 어법상 틀린 것은?

det.korean: ④ pairing → paired: 침팬지가 짝지어지는 것(수동)이므로 과거분사 paired가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ pairing(능동) → paired(수동): 실험에서 짝지어진 것(수동)
✅ ① genetically: 부사 → similar 수식
✅ ② which: 사물 선행사(device) 주격 관계대명사
✅ ③ placed: 수동 분사구문
✅ ⑤ succeeded: 과거형 동사
det.tip: 분사구문 능동/수동: 주어가 동작을 당하면 p.p.(수동)

questions.passage: It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward Wilson, an evolutionary biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today. On my way, I had trouble locating this room. Luckily, a friendly student came up to me and walked me here. It’s __________ how, in situations like this, we want to help someone in need.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "It’s + 형용사" 구문에서 상황이 흥미를 유발하므로 fascinating(흥미로운)이 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ fascinating: It’s + 형용사 → 상황 주어에 -ing형 형용사
❌ ① fascinate: 동사원형 → 문법적 불가
❌ ② fascinated: -ed형 → 사람이 느끼는 감정 (It’s 주어에 부적절)
❌ ④ fascination: 명사 → It’s + 명사 구조 부자연스러움
det.tip: It’s + 감정 형용사: 상황/사물 주어 → -ing형 (fascinating, surprising)

questions.passage: Furthermore, Dr. Hare suggested that the friendly nature of dogs probably __________ them with a survival advantage that allowed their population to grow larger than that of wolves.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: that절 내의 동사로, 주절 동사 suggested(과거)에 맞춰 과거시제 provided가 적절하다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② provided: that절 안의 과거시제 동사
❌ ① provide: 현재형 → suggested와 시제 불일치
❌ ③ providing: 분사 → 동사 자리에 부적절
❌ ④ to provide: to부정사 → 동사 자리에 부적절
det.tip: 주절이 과거(suggested) → that절도 과거(provided)로 시제 일치

questions.passage: Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and ①<u>thrived</u>. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger ②<u>communities</u> that promoted ③<u>isolation</u> and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in ④<u>smaller</u> groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a ⑤<u>competitive</u> advantage over Neanderthals.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 밑줄 친 ①~⑤ 중, 문맥상 낱말의 쓰임이 적절하지 않은 것은?

det.korean: 원문은 "promoted cooperation"(협력을 촉진). ③ isolation(고립)은 cooperation의 반의어로 부적절하다.
det.analysis:
❌ ③ isolation(고립): 원문 cooperation → "free exchange of knowledge"와 병렬 → 고립이 아닌 협력
✅ ① thrived(번성했다): 원문 일치
✅ ② communities(공동체): 원문 일치
✅ ④ smaller(더 작은): 원문 일치
✅ ⑤ competitive(경쟁적): 원문 일치
det.tip: cooperation(협력) ↔ isolation(고립) — "free exchange of knowledge"와 함께 나오므로 협력이 적절

questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: __________ is the key to success. Isn’t that a comforting thought?
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: 경쟁 사회에서 강한 자만 살아남는다는 통념에 대한 "대안적 견해(alternative view)"로 친절(kindness)이 성공의 열쇠라고 제안한다.
det.analysis:
✅ ③ kindness: "alternative view" → 강함이 아닌 친절이 성공의 열쇠
❌ ① competition: "alternative"가 아닌 기존 관점
❌ ② strength: biggest/strongest와 같은 맥락 → 대안이 아님
❌ ④ intelligence: 언급 없음
❌ ⑤ independence: 언급 없음
det.tip: "alternative view" = 기존 관점(강함)의 대안 → kindness(친절)

questions.passage: To answer these questions, I’d like to tell you about my childhood companion dog, Sparky. When we played with a ball, I noticed that he responded well to my __________.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 들어갈 말로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: Sparky는 주인의 몸짓(gestures)에 잘 반응했다. 이후 본문에서 개의 인간 몸짓에 대한 반응이 핵심 주제로 이어진다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② gestures: 본문의 핵심 주제 = 몸짓에 대한 반응
❌ ① commands: 명령은 이 글의 초점이 아님
❌ ③ speeches: 말/연설은 개와의 놀이 맥락에 부적절
❌ ④ emotions: 감정에 대한 반응은 이 글의 주제가 아님
det.tip: responded well to → 반응의 대상 + 이후 dog vs wolf 실험의 주제 = gestures

questions.passage: It’s good to see you, everyone! I’m Dr. Edward Wilson, an __________ (evolution) biologist. Thank you for inviting me here today.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: evolution(명사) → evolutionary(형용사): 명사 biologist를 수식하는 형용사 필요
det.analysis:
evolution(명사) → evolutionary(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 biologist(명사)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요
det.tip: evolution → evolutionary / revolution → revolutionary — -tion → -tionary 형용사화

questions.passage: I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their __________ (cooperate) behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 빈칸에 괄호 안의 단어를 어법에 맞게 변형하여 쓰시오.

det.korean: cooperate(동사) → cooperative(형용사): 명사 behavior를 수식하는 형용사 필요
det.analysis:
cooperate(동사) → cooperative(형용사)
빈칸 뒤 behavior(명사)를 수식하는 형용사가 필요
cooperative behavior = 협력적 행동
det.tip: cooperate → cooperative / compete → competitive — 동사 → -ive/-ative 형용사화

questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare. He conducted an experiment to see how dogs would respond to human gestures compared to wolves, who share the same common ancestor.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 개와 늑대가 공유하는 것을 본문에서 1단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "wolves, who share the same common ancestor" → 공통 조상 = ancestor
det.analysis:
개와 늑대가 공유하는 것 = the same common ancestor
1단어 답 = ancestor
det.tip: common ancestor = 공통 조상 — share the same common ancestor = 같은 공통 조상을 공유하다

questions.passage: One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge, while Neanderthals tended to live in smaller groups. These social differences may have given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals, allowing them to adapt to an ever-changing environment.
questions.stem: 다음 글에서 사회적 차이가 호모 사피엔스에게 제공한 것을 본문에서 2단어로 찾아 쓰시오.

det.korean: "given Homo sapiens a competitive advantage over Neanderthals" → 경쟁적 이점
det.analysis:
사회적 차이가 제공한 것 = competitive advantage
2단어 답 = competitive advantage
det.tip: competitive advantage = 경쟁적 우위/이점 — given A a B over C = C에 비해 A에게 B를 주다

questions.passage: I’ll give you another example of how friendliness is related to survival. Dr. Hare and his colleagues designed an experiment with chimpanzees and bonobos. Although the two are genetically similar, they are different in nature. To study their cooperative behavior, Dr. Hare’s team set up a device which required two individuals to pull both ends of a rope at the same time in order to access food on a board. When placed with partners that the chimpanzees knew, they were able to work together to get the food. However, when paired with new partners, the chimpanzees usually failed to get the food, and when they occasionally succeeded, they did not share the food with their partner. The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하는 것은?

det.korean: "They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with" → 보노보는 어떤 개체와 짝을 이루든 문제를 해결했다.
det.analysis:
✅ ② 보노보는 어떤 개체와도 문제 해결: 원문 "regardless of which individual" 일치
❌ ① 침팬지는 새 짝과 실패: "usually failed"
❌ ③ 본질적으로 같다: "different in nature"
❌ ④ 보노보는 나눔 거부: "more willing to share"
det.tip: 내용 일치: regardless of = ~에 상관없이 → 어떤 짝과도 성공

ch: 보노보는 어떤 개체와 짝을 이루든 문제를 해결했다.
침팬지와 보노보는 본질적으로 같은 성격을 가진다.

questions.passage: Now let’s turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Neanderthals were able to make tools and fire and had strong bodies with well-developed muscles and broad shoulders. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived.
questions.stem: 다음 글의 내용과 일치하지 않는 것은?

det.korean: 본문: "it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived" → 호모 사피엔스가 살아남았다. 따라서 "호모 사피엔스가 먼저 멸종했다"는 반대.
det.analysis:
❌ ④ 호모 사피엔스가 먼저 멸종: 원문과 정반대 → "Homo sapiens survived and thrived"
✅ ① "physically superior" → 일치
✅ ② "larger communities" → 일치
✅ ③ "make tools and fire" → 일치
det.tip: 불일치 문제: 핵심 사실(누가 생존했는가)을 정확히 파악

ch: 호모 사피엔스의 조상들은 더 큰 공동체에서 살았다.
네안데르탈인은 도구와 불을 만들 수 있었다.

questions.passage: In our competitive society, many people believe that only the biggest or the strongest can survive and thrive. However, I propose an alternative view: kindness is the key to success. Isn’t that a comforting thought? We can use the power of our natural kindness to communicate and cooperate with different individuals. We can all benefit from this instead of trying to be better than others.
questions.stem: 이 글(강연) 전체의 목적으로 가장 적절한 것은?

det.korean: "kindness is the key to success" + 개/보노보/호모 사피엔스의 예시 → 다정함과 협력이 생존의 핵심
det.analysis:
✅ ③ 다정함과 협력이 생존의 핵심: "kindness is the key to success"
❌ ① 경쟁의 중요성: 오히려 이에 반대
❌ ② 동물 실험 윤리: 언급 없음
❌ ④ 네안데르탈인 소개: 예시일 뿐 목적 아님
det.tip: 강연의 목적: 결론부 "kindness is the key to success"가 핵심 주장

ch: 동물 실험의 윤리적 문제를 제기하기 위해
다정함과 협력이 생존의 핵심임을 주장하기 위해

questions.passage: The responsive behavior of dogs also caught the attention of an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Brian Hare is an evolutionary anthropologist."

det.korean: "an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare" → Brian Hare는 진화 인류학자이다. → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: 본문 "an evolutionary anthropologist, Brian Hare"와 정확히 일치
det.tip: 직업/신분 확인: 본문에서 명시된 표현과 진술을 대조

questions.passage: The bonobos, on the other hand, got along much better than the chimpanzees. They solved the problem regardless of which individual they were paired with, and they were also more willing to share the food. This research shows that bonobos have a cooperative and friendly nature.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Bonobos refused to share food with unfamiliar partners."

det.korean: 본문: "they were also more willing to share the food" → 보노보는 더 기꺼이 음식을 나누었다. "거부했다(refused)"는 False.
det.analysis: ❌ False: "more willing to share" ≠ "refused to share" → 정반대
det.tip: willing(기꺼이 하는) ↔ refused(거부한) — 의미가 정반대

questions.passage: Now let’s turn our attention to ourselves, Homo sapiens. How have we managed to survive for so long? Neanderthals existed together with Homo sapiens until about 40,000 years ago, and they were known to be intelligent and physically superior to Homo sapiens. Despite these attributes, however, it was Homo sapiens who ultimately survived and thrived. One possible explanation is that our ancestors lived in larger communities that promoted cooperation and the free exchange of knowledge.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"Homo sapiens survived because they were physically stronger than Neanderthals."

det.korean: 본문: 네안데르탈인이 "physically superior"했다. 호모 사피엔스 생존 이유는 큰 공동체와 협력이지 신체적 힘이 아니다. → False
det.analysis:
❌ False: 원문 "Neanderthals were physically superior" → 신체적으로는 네안데르탈인이 우월
호모 사피엔스 생존 이유 = 큰 공동체 + 협력 + 지식 교환
det.tip: 인과 관계 파악: 생존 이유 ≠ 신체적 힘 → 사회적 협력과 지식 교환

questions.passage: I’d like to end this talk with a message. Think of our society as a bouquet. Just as each flower adds to the beauty when it harmonizes with the others, each person can contribute to a more beautiful world when they cooperate.
questions.stem:
다음 진술이 본문의 내용과 일치하면 True, 일치하지 않으면 False를 고르시오.

"The speaker compares society to a bouquet."

det.korean: "Think of our society as a bouquet" → 우리 사회를 꽃다발에 비유 → True
det.analysis: ✅ True: "Think of our society as a bouquet" → 사회를 꽃다발에 비유
det.tip: Think of A as B = A를 B로 비유하다 → compare A to B와 같은 의미
